The classic game of LUDO is now a book!
Since starting the PlayBook’d series, we have had many requests to design LUDO and now we have. After a couple of iterations, I landed on this design that lets the colorful pieces really stand out on the covers and the pages.
LUDO is simple to learn, but every turn can change the game. Race your pieces around the board, send opponents back to start, and try to be the first player to bring all your pieces safely home.
Disguised as a Book
This design blends right into your bookshelf, coffee table, or game shelf. But when you're ready to play, turn the page, open the book, and you're playing LUDO.
Easy Storage
No bulky box. No loose pieces scattered everywhere.
The covers hold together with magnets, keeping everything secure inside when the game is closed. The game pieces store neatly inside the book, making it easy to pack away, display, or bring with you.
How to Play
Each player chooses a color and takes the matching pieces and places them in their start.
Players take turns rolling the die.
Roll a 6 to move one of your pieces out of start and onto the board.
Move your pieces around the track toward your home lane.
If you land on a space occupied by an opponent’s piece, the opponent's piece is sent back to their start.
If you land on a space occupied by your own piece, you form a blockade. While pieces form a blockade, opponents pieces can't move through it.
Once a piece completes the full path around the board, it enters into the home lane. To enter your home you must roll an exact dice roll. (To go three spaces you need a 3)
The first player to get all of their pieces home wins.

I wanted to design a better way to hold your glasses without stretching out your shirt collar or needing a pocket, so I created the CaterClip! I am really happy with how this little guy came out.
The inchworm uses magnets glued inside his feet to attach to a leaf hidden inside your shirt. The inchworm’s body creates the perfect place to hang your glasses.
Magnetic Attachment
Place the leaf inside your shirt and attach the inchworm from the outside using the glued-in magnets. The leaf helps spread out the weight while keeping the inchworm securely in place. I tried my best to dislodge my glasses and never succeeded with this design.
Note: For this to work in any orientation, insert the magnets with oposite polarity,
Make sure to use strong N52 rated magnets!
Wear It Anywhere
The inchworm can be placed almost anywhere on your shirt, so you can position your glasses wherever they feel most comfortable and accessible.
How it Works
The curved body securely holds your glasses while making it look like a little inchworm is crawling across your shirt. It is a fun alternative to hanging your glasses from your collar, where they can stretch the fabric or easily fall off.
Easy Quick Print
This design only needs 4 magnets, 10 grams of filament and is a super fast print.
Extra Large (XL) version included
The file includes and XL version of the inchworm and leaf, incase you thick-frame sunglasses

projectDescription:
The classic game of hangman is now a book!  Since I started the Playbook'd series, i've wanted to make hangman into a book.
Hangman is the classic paper / pen game. But now you can play it in real life!
Over 50,000 words
This design includes 2 sets of the alphabet, which means you can repeat letters. Words can be up to 7 letters long. So there are nearly 52,000 english words that can be played!
Disguised as a book
This design blends in on your bookshelf or table. But when you're ready to play, turn the page, open the book, and you're playing hangman.
Easy Storage
This looks like a book when you're not playing. So you can store it anywhere! And since the covers hold together with magnets, all your pieces are secure inside. There are magnets to hold all the body parts, and slots for all the letters.
How to Play
Executioner: Pick a word up to 7 letters long. Place the letter into the slots, they will click in. The first letter of the word goes into the rightmost slot.
Guesser: Guess a letter and flip up the cover to mark it as guessed. If you get it right, the executioner reveals a letter. If you get it wrong, they add a piece to the man. (8 guesses total, starting with the rope). Win by guessing the word before the man gets hung.

Not your average Tic Tac Toe

How to Play
The board: The board is made of 9 small tic-tac-toe boards arranged in a 3×3 grid.
Forced Moves: The space you choose sends your opponent to the matching small board next turn. Example: if you play in the top-right space inside a mini-game, your opponent must play in the top-right board.
X goes first and may play anywhere on the board
On your turn, place your mark in any open space of the mini game you’re sent to.
Win a mini-game by getting 3 in a row inside it.
Once a mini-game is won, Place your win-marker on that mini game. This claims your spot on the big board.
Win the game by winning 3 mini-games in a row on the big board.
If you’re sent to a board that is already won or full, you may play in any open board.
If a small board fills with no winner, it becomes a tie and no one claims it.

To "deploy" the game, open the book and stand it up on the covers. The scoring plank will automatically drop down. After it does, move the pawn to the center circle. Then, pull up on the collapsible tower until it locks into place. Make sure the arms are in-line with the length of the spine. Then, rotate the arms up, and play! Start with the pawn in the middle circle of the tray. The game beings after a 3 - 2 - 1 - GO!  Then race see who can swing their ring onto the hook. Once you get your ring onto your hook, you may advance the pawn 1 circle closer to your oppenent. But be quick, because they can move it back towards you if they get their ring on the hook. Keep going until the pawn "walks the plank" off the final circle. The player who advances all the way off their opponents side of the plank wins.
